craft_notes: Sthāyin: definition — two names, one substance. Sanskrit-first: ca twice (bathing-AND-purity linked, not equalled); samāveśaḥ nom. pred: purity IS immersion. Rows: 9 (name→substance pair), 1 ('own form' closes — svarūpa end-weight), 12 (definition settles, no performance yet). Close: 'entering the Supreme Lord's own form.' Rejected: quoting L2's 'immersion' sentence — killed: zero-shared-L2 rule (reworded to saṃviṣ 'entering'); 'baptism' — killed: snāna kept bath. Read aloud: BATH-ing IS-called PU-ri-ty — AND-pu-ri-TY is-EN-ter-ing THE-SU-preme-LORD's OWN-form.

lines: and purity is entering the Supreme Lord's own form.
l4.sanskrit_cite: snānaṃ ca śuddhatā ucyate śuddhatā ca parameśvarasvarūpasamāveśaḥ

reads_against.argmap: What is bathing called, and what is it? → Snāna is defined twice over: named purity, and purity itself is samāveśa in the Lord's own svarūpa — water-rite and identity-collapse are one word.
c1_essence: Bathing names purity; purity is immersion in the Supreme Lord's own form.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vidhi weight (quiescence carrying ritual order)
